near_miss.lead: weave cunning: ON vafist (vefja) ~ Gk μῆτιν ὕφαινον
near_miss.why_not: The ON form is vefja 'wrap, entangle' (reflexive 'margur í vafist' = 'many got entangled in it'), not vefa 'weave', and there is no object meaning plan or cunning. The congruence is only the root *webʰ- and there is no figure 'weave a plan'.
The Greek and Latin partners just have 'foot' in unrelated contexts (footprint, measure). 'Trample under foot' is a generic Christian/Latinate idiom in Árna saga.

near_miss.lead: women milking: ON konur ... mjólka ~ MIr. bó blicht ... ben
near_miss.why_not: MIr. blicht is the noun 'milk(-yield)' of a cow, listed next to 'every woman' as a tribute, while ON is about women who can barely milk because of a bull. The words *h2melg- and *gwen- are cognate but there is no shared syntax or context, and milking by women is everyday matter.

near_miss.lead: the replaceable/irreplaceable kin topos: ON fá mér aðra móður eða föður / önnur móðir betri eða faðir ~ Hdt. πατρὸς δὲ καὶ μητρὸς ... ἀδελφεὸς ἂν ἄλλος οὐδενὶ τρόπῳ γένοιτο (Intaphernes' wife; cf. Soph. Ant. 905ff., recalled)
near_miss.why_not: Finnbogi's words are about foster parents versus birth parents ('you act as if you could get me another mother or father'), not the logic that a sibling cannot be replaced once the parents are dead. 'Another' is not cognate (annarr < *h2énteros vs ἄλλος < *h2élyos), and father plus mother is universal. This is a folklore motif at most, not shared wording. The AV partners (pitā ca mātā ca vidma; pitā putrau mātaraṃ muñca) are generic kin lists.
ON 'went to visit her father and mother' versus the AV earth-mother/Parjanya-father hymn. Kin terms only, with no shared figure.

near_miss.lead: pitṛbandhu mātṛbandhu ~ πατρὸς καὶ μητρὸς τῆς αὐτῆς
near_miss.why_not: The pairing of father's and mother's kin is generic, and the ON pivot is a plain genealogy.

near_miss.lead: two hundred: ON Tvö hundruð ~ RV dvé ... śaté góḥ
near_miss.why_not: ON is the dying miser's muttered 'two hundred in the ravine' (hidden silver), RV is a dānastuti count of cows. The numeral pair is cognate but generic, with no shared context.
Counting with ordinals is not phraseology. The ON lists seven sons, Herodotus the seven walls of Ecbatana; this is coincidental enumeration.

near_miss.lead: frost and wind: ON frost né vind ~ Lat. uenti ... pruinae
near_miss.why_not: ON frost and Lat. pruina (*prews-) and vindr/ventus (*h2weh1nt-) are genuinely cognate, but in an ON negated pair 'lacked neither frost nor wind' against a Lucretian catalogue of meteorological phenomena. Weather words co-occur generically. No pair-specific syntax.

near_miss.lead: murky night: ON myrkt af nótt ~ SCr. mrkla noć / noć puna mraka (*mergw- + *nokwts)
near_miss.why_not: Searched (*mergw- + *nokwts, near 4): 29 Germanic hits, all ON prose (the saga formula 'myrkt (var/gerði) af nótt' in Egils, Grettis, Jómsvíkinga, Finnboga, Þiðreks saga and others), 2 Slavic (only these Vuk lines), and none elsewhere (no OE, Edda, byliny or Old Russian). *mergw- 'dark' is a Germanic–Slavic(–Baltic) lexeme, so any 'dark night' in both is automatically cognate. The collocation is semantically trivial, the syntax differs (ON impersonal 'it grew dark of night' vs SCr. epithet/genitive), and the Vuk material is late.

near_miss.lead: wolf-and-ears proverb: ON Þaðan er mér úlfs von er eg eyrun sé (also Fáfnismál 35, recalled) ~ Gk proverb τὸν λύκον τῶν ὤτων ἔχειν/λαβεῖν (Polybius 30.20.8, Plutarch Praec. 802d, found by search; Lat. auribus teneo lupum, Ter. Phorm. 506, recalled)
near_miss.why_not: The slab partner is only the name Λύκος. The Greek/Latin proverb found by search ('hold the wolf by the ears' = an inescapable dilemma) has a different verb and a different sense from the ON 'where I see ears I expect the wolf' (recognizing from signs). The wolf's ears are a naturally salient detail, so sharing only *wlkwos + *h2ows is not enough to defend a common proverb.

near_miss.lead: cow-slaying *gwhen- + *gwows: ON kýr særðar til bana ~ Ved. gāṃ han-
near_miss.why_not: ON has bani as a noun in the stock phrase 'til bana' ('to death') with kýr as subject of a passive participle, not verb plus object. Ved. 'if you kill our cow, horse, man' is a curse formula and Rām. 'kick a sleeping cow' is a sin list. The contexts are not congruent and the cognate match is incidental.

error.correct_reading: Λύκος, personal name (Γνούρου τοῦ Λύκου τοῦ Σπαργαπείθεος), should be marked (name) and unmapped
Κατάνη, city name (Catana), should be unmapped
Skíði, personal name (subject of flutti á brott), not skíð 'ski/stick'
error.evidence: Skíði flutti á brott að óvilja Ásbjarnar föður hennar

note: Second reader on 14 flagged bundles. No claims: all leads are generic or have incongruent contexts. Searched murky night (*mergw-+*nokwts) and wolf+ears (*wlkwos+*h2ows) across corpora.
